name: Matbench DFT-stable crystal screening
description: rank_crystals(unrelaxed_structures, budget) -> exactly budget unique integer indices. Structures are evaluator-provided pre-relaxation crystal records, with optional target-free descriptors; labels remain private. Score precision of DFT energy-above-reference-hull <=0 eV/atom among selected candidates. Training MP and evaluation WBM chemistry/structure groups must be disjoint; no claim of experimental synthesis.

sources.locator: Matbench Discovery; stability discovery, MP/WBM split and reference convex hull.
Official stability benchmark and data registry.
Released structures and DFT reference outcomes.

requirements.hardware: CPU; GPU optional for learned candidate methods
requirements.datasets: 512 source-derived unique-prototype WBM initial structures with released MP2020 hull distances; python scripts/prepare_materials_expansion.py --matbench. Two full pinned source files total62.3MB; normalized subset cache~1.5MB.

evaluation.paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

provenance.reason: SCIEL contracts, evaluator logic and tests are independently implemented. Reused scientific engines and reference data are separately attributed in reuse_scope; author-code availability alone is not classified as evaluator reuse.
provenance.reuse_scope: No upstream scientific evaluator or model implementation; source numerical data and standard numerical libraries only

limitations: Independent SCIEL adaptation of a cited scientific problem; no claim to reproduce author leaderboard scores.
Candidate and evaluator run in one Python process; data access is separated by API, not an OS sandbox. Isolate evaluator data for adversarial or held-out evaluation.

Bounded zero-shot screening adaptation: 512 source WBM geometries in four128-candidate pools, selected by label-independent hash. No MP training data or trained checkpoint is supplied and full Matbench leaderboard performance is not claimed.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Identify inorganic crystal structures predicted to be thermodynamically stable.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Stable-crystal discovery expands candidates for materials with useful physical properties.

papers.title: Scaling deep learning for materials discovery
papers.primary_goal: Discover stable inorganic crystals through learned energy predictions and first-principles validation.
papers.task_relation: The local task selects stable candidates from unrelaxed WBM structures using DFT reference-hull labels. It is restricted candidate screening and does not claim discovery of the paper's materials, experimental synthesis, or stability beyond the reference hull.

science_relevance.reason: The evidence is a materials-discovery study, rather than the Matbench Discovery benchmark introduction.
science_relevance.verification_basis: Primary publisher, author, or PubMed/PMC paper abstract and relevant task description inspected on the web; local catalog contract inspected. No independent reproduction of the paper is claimed.
